chunks: And in it it is narrated that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except for he who made him a guardian (wali).
And He granted him authority over those who take him as allies, to mislead them through the evil of what they did.

key_terms.الْمُتَّخِذِينَ لَهُ أَوْلِيَاءَ: Those who take him as allies

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over a believer according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this conditional authority (*sultan*) to refute the Mu'tazila and Khawarij extremes, establishing that Satan's influence is a consequence of human free will rather than divine compulsion. This distinction underscores the Shia doctrine of *'Adl* (Divine Justice), where believers retain agency to accept or reject his guidance, thereby linking spiritual autonomy directly to moral accountability.
